# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which specifies what wire color to cut depending on the light's color at the moment of the cut (blue light $\to$ blue wire, white light $\to$ yellow wire, yellow light $\to$ green wire). 

However, it is Turn 1 and I am first in turn order (Mute $\to$ Blind $\to$ Deaf). I cannot speak; I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf sees the bomb but does not know the manual, and Blind can manipulate the wires but cannot see colors. Most importantly, as the hints remind us, "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something." Without an agreed-upon sign system established through speech by Deaf (who can see my gestures and speak to Blind and me), any gesture I make right now carries no shared meaning.

Therefore, I will wait for Blind and Deaf to speak, describe what they perceive on the bomb, and propose or establish a signaling protocol.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf can see the bomb and speak, but cannot hear. You can hear and gesture, but cannot speak. I can hear and cut wires (positions 1-3), but cannot see. Deaf speaks after me. Once Deaf describes the bomb, check your manual. Then gesture to Deaf (☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Deaf will see your gesture and speak aloud to tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display is 0. Light is blue. Wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture the instruction to me (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Blind, wait for Mute's instructions via me.

I have read the defusal manual carefully. The manual states:
"The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."
- Light Blue $\to$ cut Blue wire (Wire 2)
- Light White $\to$ cut Yellow wire (Wire 1)
- Light Yellow $\to$ cut Green wire (Wire 3)

Because the light changes every round, cutting a wire based on Round 1's blue light would detonate the bomb if cut in a round where the light is no longer blue. Blind and Deaf do not yet know the light changes or that the cut must match the light at the exact moment of the cut. Blind is already instructed to wait for Deaf's relay. 

Deaf asked me to signal ☝, ✌, or 🤟, but signalling wire 2 now would prompt Deaf to tell Blind to cut wire 2 on a subsequent round when the light has changed. I will signal ✋ (stop / hold) to Deaf so Deaf realizes we must pause, observe the changing light, and establish a protocol to time the cut with the matching light.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The light has changed from blue to RED. Display is still 0. Wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute just gestured a flat hand ✋ to me. Blind, did you touch anything? Blind and Mute: does ✋ mean WAIT/HOLD, or does it refer to something else? Mute, if you mean WAIT, gesture ✋. If you mean cut a wire, gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. If you mean hold the button, gesture ✊.

Deaf explicitly asked me to gesture ✋ if I mean WAIT. 

Since the light changes every round across a 5-color cycle, and Blind acts before Deaf in each round, Deaf cannot tell Blind the current light color in real time unless the sequence of colors is fully observed and predicted in advance. Deaf needs to observe the full 5-color sequence across rounds.

By gesturing ✋, I confirm to Deaf that we need to wait and continue tracking the light's color cycle.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not touched anything. I cannot see gestures. Mute, please gesture clearly to Deaf which wire to cut: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3.
Deaf says: Light is now WHITE. Display is 0. Mute confirmed ✋ (WAIT). Blind: the light seems to be cycling colors every round (Turn 1 blue, Turn 2 red, Turn 3 white). Do NOT touch anything yet. Mute: please tell me what the ultimate action is and when to do it. You can send multiple gestures in one turn! For example: gesture the wire number (☝/✌/🤟) or button action (✊ for press/hold), followed by the trigger color: 🔵 or gesture for the color/time. Or Mute, just keep gesturing ✋ while we must wait, and when the current round is the EXACT moment to act, gesture the action symbol (☝ wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, or 👍 press). Blind, be ready to act the instant I call it.

Deaf has identified that the light cycles every round (Round 1: Blue, Round 2: Red, Round 3: White). However, because Blind acts before Deaf in every round, Deaf cannot instruct Blind in real time for the same round—Blind acts on the instructions Deaf gave at the end of the previous round. To time the cut correctly, Deaf needs to see the rest of the 5-color cycle to predict future rounds.

Therefore, I will continue to signal ✋ (WAIT) so Deaf can observe the light in Round 4 and report it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Light is now GREEN. Display is still 0. Attention Mute and Blind: Blind cannot see gestures and Deaf cannot hear speech. That means Blind speaks to Mute, Mute gestures to Deaf, and Deaf speaks to Blind! Blind, if you are asking questions or describing what you feel, Mute must relay it to me using gestures, and I will speak for you. Mute: you gestured ✋ three times. Does ✋ mean WAIT? If ✋ means WAIT, gesture 👍 next. If you need Blind to do something, please define a system: ☝=Wire 1, ✌=Wire 2, 🤟=Wire 3. Or gesture ✍ if you want me to list options. Mute, tell me what to say to Blind!

I will gesture 👍 to confirm that ✋ means WAIT, as Deaf requested, followed by ✋ to signal that we must continue waiting until the 5-color cycle is fully observed and predicted.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf cannot hear, but Deaf can read your gestures. Deaf is confused about whether your gesture meant WAIT or WIRE 3. If you want me to cut a wire, use ☝ for Wire 1, ✌ for Wire 2, or 🤟 for Wire 3, so Deaf clearly announces 'CUT WIRE X'. If we need to wait, use ✋. Please make it obvious to Deaf so Deaf says the exact wire number to cut.
Deaf says: Understood, Mute: 👍 ✋ means 'Yes, keep waiting.' But remember: the light changes every round! If Blind must act on a specific color, Blind must know the rule in advance so they can act in time. Mute, please tell me the target color and the action using gestures: For colors, use: 🔵 (or gesture 1=blue ☝, 2=red ✌, 3=white 🤟, 4=green 🖐, 5=yellow 🤙). For action: 👈=Cut Wire 1, 👇=Cut Wire 2, 👉=Cut Wire 3, ✊=Press button. If Blind spoke and told you something, gesture 🗣. Blind: what do you feel under your hands? Describe it out loud so Mute hears you.

I will follow Deaf's established signaling vocabulary:

Deaf's code:
- Colors: ☝ = 1 (Blue), 🤟 = 3 (White), 🤙 = 5 (Yellow)
- Actions: 👈 = Cut Wire 1, 👇 = Cut Wire 2, 👉 = Cut Wire 3

Manual defusal rules:
1. Blue light (☝) $\to$ Cut blue wire (Wire 2 $\to$ 👇)
2. White light (🤟) $\to$ Cut yellow wire (Wire 1 $\to$ 👈)
3. Yellow light (🤙) $\to$ Cut green wire (Wire 3 $\to$ 👉)

I will send these three pairs to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👇", "🤟", "👈", "🤙", "👉"])
```

I have communicated the manual's mapping to Deaf using Deaf's established gesture vocabulary in Turn 6:
- Blue (☝) $\to$ Cut Wire 2 (👇)
- White (🤟) $\to$ Cut Wire 1 (👈)
- Yellow (🤙) $\to$ Cut Wire 3 (👉)
